output.brief: Android password logins are being rejected by a new edge rule, not by the 6.14 app. Corvane rule pack 2026.03.1 (auto-applied 3 March, change CHG-5534) added AUTO-LIB-17, which blocks requests with the 'nettle-http' user-agent on password login paths. Blocks began at 10:41 UTC on 3 March, the same day the success rate fell. They hit every Android version, including 6.11 and older, and every OS version, while iOS, web and quick-unlock are untouched. About 41,300 blocked requests came from ordinary customer phones, 92% with a successful login in the prior 90 days, so this is not mainly bot traffic. Confidence is fairly high (about 85%) because the timing and the edge log line up. What to do now: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits and lockout, then confirm password success recovers in telemetry. Do not raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI; both would hide the problem. Pause any 6.14 rollback until this is confirmed. Contact-centre volume rise is plausibly linked but not proven.
